title: Compute brief - 9 November 2026
description: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into reports that Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and the stock fell about 5% on Monday, while Anthropic kept buying physical capacity: Riot's 10-Q names it as the tenant on a $28 billion, 910 MW Corsicana lease, and the FT reports a $3.4 billion, 1.7 GW gas generator deal. Wire: Riot Corsicana, SoftBank and Grab's $1.85 billion Malaysia programme, SpaceXAI's 6 GW Arizona filing, 600,000 H200s held in Hong Kong, Israel's 300,000-GPU target, Kazakhstan's Ekibastuz phase two. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The chip CEO is under review. The buyer keeps signing for power.
lede: Nvidia's board said on Sunday it has opened an independent investigation, overseen by independent directors and outside counsel, after reports that Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort; the board says it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, and CNBC reported the stock down about 5% on Monday while AMD and other chipmakers rose. The buyers did not blink. Riot's 10-Q names Anthropic as the tenant on a 15-year, 910 MW powered land lease for its whole Corsicana, Texas campus at $130 per kW-month, about $28 billion of contract value, and the FT reports Anthropic paid about $3.4 billion for 1.7 GW of gas-fired generators. Microsoft is moving the other way on rented capacity, winding down a 2023 Oracle deal on older Nvidia hardware a day after Bloomberg reported tighter oversight of its neocloud projects; CoreWeave reports Q3 on Tuesday with its 2032 notes yielding above 16%. Live list prices held: 70 confirms, 0 ticks and 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69 after Friday's rise.
